capabilities: Compute XP and levels from daily-note checkboxes, completion bonuses and frontmatter habits
Maintain streaks with monthly freeze tokens, tier bonuses and configurable day-off rules
Award deterministic loot drops and reveal lore fragments on level-up, with swappable packs
Show progress via a sidebar widget, status-bar item or kuro-status code block embedded in notes
Chat with a self-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LM Studio, Ollama) about your day
disambiguation: Not a task manager or habit tracker; it only awards XP for tasks and habits your daily notes already record.
extras: The optional AI chat is off by default and the plugin makes no network connection while it is disabled; all XP, streak, loot and lore logic runs locally. Extended documentation (manual, troubleshooting, customization) is hosted outside the README.
motivation: The author built it for ADHD and autism, because most gamification plugins for note apps are built for neurotypical brains: punishing streaks, exponential XP curves and nagging notifications.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in progress or habit gamification, and existing gamification tools use hard streaks and nagging that penalise a missed day.

relations.evidence: If TaskNotes is installed and configured differently, Kuro offers to adopt its configuration with one click.
If you have the LLM Endpoint Manager plugin installed, the chat takes its endpoints and model from there

requires.name: API key for the chat endpoint

summary: Gamification engine that computes XP, levels, streaks with freeze tokens, loot and lore from your daily notes, with an optional local AI chat.
